previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD, CABG, COPD, CVA, and long-term alcohol abuse was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and right upper quadrant pain. Initial workup revealed elevated liver enzymes, fatty liver, and gallstones, but imaging ruled out cholecystitis. A diagnosis of alcoholic hepatitis was made, supported by clinical history and lab findings. An endoscopy showed mild esophagitis and diffuse gastritis. He was managed supportively with thiamine, folic acid, multivitamins, and acid suppression. His platelet count, which was initially low, improved during the admission, allowing restart of Plavix. Urinary incontinence was attributed to detrusor instability, and oxybutynin was restarted. Liver function tests improved steadily. He was discharged home with home health services, new medications including rifaximin, and follow-up plans with primary care, hepatology, and GI. Alcohol cessation was strongly emphasized.

Brief Hospital Course:
#Sepsis: ___ SIRS criteria met on arrival to ED, lactate 8.5.  
Abdominal pain as a possible localizing symptom, but CT with and 
without contrast was negative.  CXR and UA negative for 
infection.  No signs of end-organ damage (Cr WNL, no 
encephalopathy).  Lactate became normal after 5L NS IVF.  Pt was 
put on empiric antibiotics (vancomycin, ceftriaxone, flagyl) for 
48hrs; antibiotics were discontinued on ___ because pt 
remained afebrile and did not have leukocytosis.  Pt remained 
afebrile and w/o leukocytosis off of antibiotics.
.
#Diffuse abdominal pain/nausea/vomiting: Likely caused by 
alcoholic gastritis or exacerbation of esophagitis secondary to 
alcohol use.  Pt was started on 40 mg IV pantoprazole BID 
(outpatient PO omeprazole ineffective); home regimen of PO 
ranitidine and sucralfate were continued.  Zofran PRN nausea was 
used.  Pain was managed with PRN acetaminophen and PRN 
oxycodone.
.  
#Metabolic derangement: On arrival in the ED, pt had metabolic 
acidosis secondary to lactic acidosis with compensatory 
respiratory alkalosis, also concurrent metabolic alkalosis due 
to vomiting (RR40; ABG showing low PCO2, pH 7.5).  Anion gap 
became normal on ___.
.
#Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: Pt had documented a-fib episode 
back in ___.  During early morning ___, pt developed a-fib 
with RVR, HR in 150s; O2sat 93% on 2L.  Pt was given 5mg 
metoprolol IV x1, then 10mg diltiazem IV x1.  HR then fell to 
___.  Chest x-ray compared to prior study on ___ showed 
new bilateral pleural effusion; pt was then given 10mg IV lasix. 
 Pt was then started on 25mg PO metoprolol BID, but HR fell to 
___.  Metoprolol was therefore decreased to 12.5mg PO BID; 
however, pt continued to feel light-headed.  We therefore 
replaced metoprolol with 30mg PO diltiazem QID on ___ pt 
was asymptomatic, and HR remained ~60 on telemetry.  On ___, 
diltiazem was changed to extended release form 120mg daily.
.  
#EtOH Abuse: Patient's serum EtOH level was 118 on presentation. 
 Alcohol was a likely precipitant of gastritis/esophagitis.  Pt 
was monitored per ___ protocol; he received 5mg diazepam only 
once PRN CIWA >10 on ___, but this was felt to be unlikely 
related to alcohol withdrawal.  Pt received IV thiamine and 
folic acid daily; home PO multivitamin was continued.  A care 
coordination meeting with the pt's PCP, personal care assistant, 
and the medical team was held; abstinence from alcohol was 
emphasized throughout the hospitalization.
.
# Anemia: Hct 38.4 on admission, dropping to 25 on ___ after 
5L IVF (baseline ___.  No obvious signs of bleeding, pt 
asymptomatic.  Hct improved to 31.3 on discharge.
.
# Hypomagnesemia: Nadir of 1.3, repleted with IV MgSO4; 1.6 on 
discharge.
.
# Hypophosphatemia: Nadir of 1.2, repleted with Neutraphos; 3.2 
on discharge.
.
# COPD: Pt tachypnea on arrival to ED likely compensatory for 
metabolic acidosis.  Respiratory PE unremarkable; no acute 
process on CXR.  Pt was continued on home Spiriva and albuterol 
nebs PRN SOB.
.  
# CAD: No CP, hemodynamically stable.  ASA 81mg daily was 
started for stroke prevention given pt's cardiac history; 
clopidogrel was discontinued.  Pt was continued on his statin 
during the hospitalization.
.  
# Hypothyroidism: Home levothyroxine was continued.
.  
# Hyperlipidemia: Home rosuvastatin was continued.
.  
# FEN: IVFs / replete lytes prn / ground solids/thin liquids
# PPX: heparin SC 5,000 units TID
# ACCESS: R femoral CVL in ED, which was removed after PIV 
placed on floor.
# CODE: full
.
# Transitions in care:
-pt's clopidogrel was discontinued; ASA 81mg daily was started; 
pt also discharged on 120mg ER diltiazem
-medication reconciliation: consider whether oxybutinin can be 
discontinued (he was maintained on this during the admission, 
but we did not see any indication for it in OMR)
-f/u H. pylori titers
-continue aggressive counseling for alcohol abstinence
-continue outpatient workup for abdominal pain

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Dyspnea.

COMPARISON:  ___.

BEDSIDE FRONTAL RADIOGRAPH OF THE CHEST:  Cardiac, mediastinal and hilar
contours are normal.  Lung volumes are low with resultant bibasilar
subsegmental atelectasis.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. 
Incidental note is made of two fractured sternotomy wires.

INDICATION:  ___ male with diffuse abdominal pain and elevated
lactate.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast imaging of the abdomen and pelvis was performed. 
Multiplanar reformats were prepared and reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  

There is no consolidation in the visualized lung bases.  There is dependent
atelectasis, and unchanged mild right pleural thickening.  There is no
pericardial effusion.

Liver is diffusely low in attenuation, in keeping with fatty deposition. 
There is no focal liver lesion identified, and there is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilation.  Cholelithiasis is present without
pericholecystic inflammation to suggest acute cholecystitis.  The spleen is
normal.  There is fatty infiltration of the pancreas, without mass or ductal
dilation.  There is no hydronephrosis or nephrolithiasis.  Bilateral renal
cysts are stable.  There are no adrenal nodules or masses.

The aorta is atherosclerotic, but normal in caliber.  Mesenteric vessel
patency is not assessed without intravenous contrast.

There is thickening of the distal esophagus.  Stomach, duodenum, and
intra-abdominal loops of small bowel are normal.  There is no small bowel
obstruction or small bowel wall thickening.  There is no pneumatosis or portal
venous air.  The appendix is visualized in the right lower quadrant and is
normal (2:54).  There is extensive diverticulosis involving the left and
sigmoid colon, without acute inflammation to suggest acute diverticulitis.  

There is no free fluid.  There is no free air.  There is no mesenteric or
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:

Prostate, seminal vesicles, distal ureters, and bladder are normal.  There is
no free fluid.  There is no pelvic or inguinal adenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions concerning for
malignancy.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No acute intra-abdominal process to account for patient's abdominal pain
and elevated lactate.  Though there are no secondary signs of bowel ischemia,
there is extensive atherosclerosis, and mesenteric vessel patency cannot be
assessed without contrast.
2.  Circumferential thickening of the distal esophagus.  Further evaluation
with endoscopy is recommended.
3.  Cholelithiasis, without CT evidence of cholecystitis.
4.  Diverticulosis, without evidence of acute diverticulitis.
5.  Fatty liver.
6.  Unchanged minimal right pleural thickening.

INDICATION:  ___ male with severe abdominal pain and elevated lactate.
Evaluate for mesenteric ischemia.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis performed earlier the
same day, as well as CT abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Arterial and venous phase imaging of the abdomen and pelvis was
performed following hand injection of 150 cc of Optiray intravenous contrast
via the patient's right femoral line.  Multiplanar reformats were prepared and
reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:

Again seen is a small right pleural effusion vs pleural thickening, with
associated atelectasis.  There is no consolidation to suggest pneumonia.

There is marked thickening of the distal esophagus, as seen on prior study.

The liver remains low in attenuation, compatible with fatty infiltration. 
Hepatic and portal veins are seen to be patent on post-contrast imaging. 
There are no focal liver lesions, and there is no intra- or extra-hepatic
biliary ductal dilation.  There is cholelithiasis, without CT evidence of
acute cholecystitis.  The spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands remain
unremarkable.  There are scattered renal cysts, unchanged from prior studies,
without hydronephrosis or concerning renal mass lesion.

The aorta is atherosclerotic.  Celiac axis and SMA are patent, though there is
moderate-severe narrowing of the proximal SMA secondary to eccentric soft
plaque (2a:149).  There is normal opacification of the SMA distal, without
eveidence of embolic occlusion.  The ___ is similarly patent.

Stomach, duodenum, and intra-abdominal loops of small and large bowel are
remarkable only for sigmoid/left colonic diverticulosis.  There is no evidence
of acute diverticulitis.  Bowel wall enhances homogeneously, and there is no
pneumatosis or portal venous air.

There is no free fluid or free air.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal
adenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:

A Foley catheter is seen in the bladder.   There is no free pelvic fluid. 
There is no pelvic or inguinal adenopathy.

Atherosclerotic disease extends into the bilateral iliac vessels, with
moderately severe stenosis at the proximal left external iliac, with normal
distal vessel opacification.

A right femoral line is noted.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are degenerative changes in the spine, with no lytic or
sclerotic osseous lesions concerning for malignancy.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of mesenteric ischemia.  Aortoiliac atherosclerotic disease is
noted, with moderate-severe narrowing of the proximal SMA secondary to
eccentric soft plaque.  This is unchanged from prior studies, and there is no
evidence of embolic occlusion distally.

4.  Moderate stenosis in the proximal left external iliac artery.

2.  Redemonstration of distal esophageal thickening, for which correlation
with endoscopy is advised.

3.  Unchanged small right pleural effusion, fatty liver, renal cysts,
cholelithiasis, and diverticulosis.
